digest.component_or_area: Jira reconciler rich-text cutover with state echo suppression and concurrency conflict safety
propositions: DC and Cloud send paths must route to rich codecs (ADF and wiki-rendered) with state-based echo suppression via baseline diff rather than round-trip identity check, because DC codec is lossy (decode(encode(x)) != x).

Baseline compares must normalize the local side through normalize_outbound(fit_outbound(local)) to match decode(baseline_wire), while emit compares remain unchanged (normalize_outbound(fit_outbound(local)) vs decode_inbound(remote_wire)), so a no-edit body stays suppressed across passes.

An 8-byte change-gated rich_sha stored inline in the binding tracks whether the rendered wire has changed; when the same wire persists at reemit threshold (2), a single GET read-back overlays the synced_fields and only _advance_baselines writes to baseline, maintaining sole-writer invariant.

Both DC create sites (_map_local_to_dc_fields and _issues._translate_create_fields) must compose to_wire(fit_outbound(...)) or they ship unrendered Markdown on CREATE while updates ship rendered wiki.

The rich_text_cutover flag defaults OFF and gates both Cloud and DC send paths; when OFF the plain/identity wire path is byte-identical to before cutover, and with the marklas extra absent the cutover degrades to plain-text ADF via lazy import fallback.

Concurrent both-sides body edits are unchanged (local-wins, a713) with conflict alert emitted; Jira-authored constructs (panels, mentions, dates) survive edit-free passes under origin-gating (local != baseline); combined-mark 2-cycles are canonicalized and HTML comments self-verify with fallback.
